item.title: Dia Mirza reveals 'time slows down when I’m with my boys'
item.description: Mumbai: Actress Dia Mirza used social media to cherish the time when she stood before history, art, and architecture with her two boys- husband Vaibhav Rekhi and son Avyaan. The 'Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein' actress posted a couple of photos with Vaibhav and Avyaan from what seemed to be a museum visit. Dia shared that time slows down for her whenever she is with her boys. item.description: Dwarka/Sasan Gir: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel on Thursday visited the Dwarkadhish Temple in Dwarka and travelled to Sasan Gir, where he reviewed wildlife conservation arrangements, undertook a jungle safari and flagged off vehicles for forest personnel. item.description: New Delhi: Digital addiction is growing as a significant health problem among children and the youth and is also contributing to the mental health crisis in the country, said the government on Thursday in the Economic Survey 2025-26. item.title: High-security Punjab and Haryana Civil Secretariat gets bomb threat email
item.description: Chandigarh: The high-security Punjab and Haryana Civil Secretariat, guarded by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), was evacuated on Thursday after a bomb threat email was received in the office of the National Informatics Centre (NIC), officials said. item.title: MP: Beating retreat today, only state in India to organise the event
item.description: Bhopal: Madhya Pradesh will bring its Republic Day festivities to a ceremonial close today with the traditional Beating the Retreat ceremony at Lal Parade Ground in Jahangirabad, Bhopal. The event is scheduled to begin at 4.30 p.m. with Governor Mangubhai Patel attending as the chief guest. This grand military tradition, steeped in history, is uniquely observed in the state capital alongside the national ceremony in New Delhi. item.title: Hyderabad Police Deny Rise in Chain Snatching Incidents
item.description: Hyderabad City Police Commissioner Sajjanar has dismissed social media claims that chain snatching incidents have surged due to rising gold prices, alleging that interstate gangs have established bases in the city. He described these reports as entirely false. In a message posted on 'X' (formerly Twitter), he urged the public not to believe such rumours.
